releases.body:
tasteskill v2 is a new default skill, not an edit of the old one. It gives a coding agent an art direction, real pictures and a way to check its own work in a real browser.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

The install name did not change. Needs Node 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. Installs nothing, uses no API keys.

## What is new

- **A library instead of adjectives.** Built from a study of 247 curated sites: 20 directions, 48 hero compositions, 172 section layouts, 44 type systems, 56 palettes.
- **A script deals the direction.** `scripts/draw.mjs` deals three directions; the agent picks the one that can carry something only this client has.
- **Real pictures.** `scripts/assets.mjs` finds photographs, maps and footage of the subject's world in open collections, downloads them and records the credits.
- **A real-browser inspector.** `scripts/inspect.mjs` opens the page at 1440, 768 and 390 px and fails it on eyebrow labels, hairlines, gradients, resting shadows, headlines over two lines, empty screens and covered text.

**Taste Skill** is a set of Agent Skills that make coding agents design websites instead of assembling the average landing page. The default skill gives the agent an art direction, real pictures and a way to check its own work in a real browser. Pages it has built, each from one brief:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0).

Install · How it works · Skills · FAQ · Sponsors · License

## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill ``` That installs every skill in this repo with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. To install one, pass its install name: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` The default skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium**. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Finding pictures needs network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. Every skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so they do not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skills are loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skills into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates them in place. `./install.sh --list` shows every install name.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again. The install name did not change, and the older versions stay available under their own names (see [Skills](#skills)). ## How v2 works The default skill is built from a study of 247 curated sites. A build runs in six steps: 1. Reads the brief and lists what only this client has. 2. A script deals three of 20 researched directions and the agent picks one. 3. Finds the idea: one sentence tying the client's own material to that direction. 4. Builds with real pictures and footage from open collections, credited. 5. Checks the page in a real browser at three widths and fails it on slop. 6. Looks at its own screenshots and fixes the top three problems, up to three rounds. A build takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens. Details are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the [study](skills/taste-skill/references/research.md). ## Skills Each skill does one job. You do not need all of them. The **install name** is the value you pass to `--skill`. | Skill | Install name | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | **[taste-skill](skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md)** | `design-taste-frontend` | v2. Art direction for landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios and product pages, in any stack. Works as described above. |
Skills for a specific job (8) | Skill | Install name | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | **[redesign-skill](skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md)** | `redesign-existing-projects` | Existing projects: audit the UI first, then fix layout, spacing, hierarchy and styling. | | **[image-to-code-skill](skills/image-to-code-skill/SKILL.md)** | `image-to-code` | Generate site references, analyse them, then build the frontend to match. | | **[gpt-tasteskill](skills/gpt-tasteskill/SKILL.md)** | `gpt-taste` | A stricter variant for GPT and Codex: more layout variance, stronger motion direction. | | **[soft-skill](skills/soft-skill/SKILL.md)** | `high-end-visual-design` | Calm, polished UI: soft contrast, whitespace, spring motion. | | **[minimalist-skill](skills/minimalist-skill/SKILL.md)** | `minimalist-ui` | Editorial product UI with a restrained palette and crisp structure. | | **[brutalist-skill](skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md)** | `industrial-brutalist-ui` | Hard mechanical language: Swiss type, sharp contrast, experimental layout. | | **[stitch-skill](skills/stitch-skill/SKILL.md)** | `stitch-design-taste` | Rules for Google Stitch, with an optional `DESIGN.md` export. | | **[output-skill](skills/output-skill/SKILL.md)** | `full-output-enforcement` | For when the model ships half-finished work: full output, no placeholder comments. |

Install

That installs every skill in this repo with the npx skills CLI. To install one, pass its install name:

npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"

The default skill runs its scripts with Node 22+ and an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Finding pictures needs network access.

How v2 works

The default skill is built from a study of 247 curated sites. A build runs in six steps:

  1. Reads the brief and lists what only this client has.
  2. A script deals three of 20 researched directions and the agent picks one.
  3. Finds the idea: one sentence tying the client's own material to that direction.
  4. Builds with real pictures and footage from open collections, credited.
  5. Checks the page in a real browser at three widths and fails it on slop.
  6. Looks at its own screenshots and fixes the top three problems, up to three rounds.

A build takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens. Details are in the changelog and the study.

Skills

Each skill does one job. You do not need all of them. The install name is the value you pass to --skill.

Skill Install name What it does
taste-skill design-taste-frontend v2. Art direction for landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios and product pages, in any stack. Works as described above.
Skills for a specific job (8)
Skill Install name What it does
redesign-skill redesign-existing-projects Existing projects: audit the UI first, then fix layout, spacing, hierarchy and styling.
image-to-code-skill image-to-code Generate site references, analyse them, then build the frontend to match.

Image generation skills (3)

These produce design images only, no code. Use them with ChatGPT Images, Codex image mode or any agent that generates images, then hand the frames to your coding agent.

Skill Install name What it does
imagegen-frontend-web imagegen-frontend-web Website comps: hero, landing page, multi-section.
imagegen-frontend-mobile imagegen-frontend-mobile Mobile screens and flows for iOS, Android and cross-platform.
brandkit brandkit Brand-kit boards: logo directions, palettes, type, applications.

Which one should I use?

  • Building a new public page: taste-skill.
  • Improving a page that already exists: redesign-skill.
  • The visual direction is already decided: soft-skill, minimalist-skill or brutalist-skill.
  • You want images first, then code: an image-generation skill, or image-to-code-skill for the whole pipeline in one go.
  • The agent keeps cutting its output short: add output-skill.
Older versions of taste-skill

Kept for projects that depend on their exact behaviour.

Skill Install name What it is
taste-skill-v2-experimental design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental The single-file, dial-driven rewrite that was the default before v2.
taste-skill-v1 design-taste-frontend-v1 The original. 
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental"
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend-v1"

Both have three 1 to 10 dials at the top of the file: DESIGN_VARIANCE (centred and clean to asymmetric), MOTION_INTENSITY (hover only to scroll-driven) and VISUAL_DENSITY (spacious to dense). v2 has no dials. Its direction comes from the draw and its limits from the inspector.

Common Questions

What does the default skill need?
Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. It installs nothing and uses no API keys. It needs the internet only to find pictures.

Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?
From open collections such as Wikimedia Commons, Openverse and the Met. Only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA files are offered, and the skill puts the credits on the page. Replace them with your own when you have them.

Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?
Yes. The rules are about design, not a framework.

Is it for dashboards and app screens?
No. The default skill is for public-facing pages. Use minimalist-skill or soft-skill for product UI.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An anti-slop frontend framework and skill set designed to prevent AI agents from generating generic, poorly designed UI.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Taste-Skill acts as an anti-slop frontend framework intended to elevate the design quality of code generated by AI agents. It addresses the common issue where LLMs produce generic, visually unappealing, or heavily boilerplate UIs by providing a curated set of design rules and constraints. The project functions as a specific 'skill' that can be injected into agentic workflows to guide styling, layout, and component choices. By enforcing strong design opinions and best practices, it ensures the resulting frontends look premium and bespoke rather than obviously machine-generated. It effectively gives the AI a sense of 'good taste' in modern web design.
keyFeatures: Anti-Slop Directives: Prevents the generation of generic, overused UI patterns and standard Bootstrap-style layouts.
Design Opinionation: Enforces strong, modern design principles regarding typography, spacing, and color palettes.
Agent Skill Integration: Designed to be easily consumed and executed by autonomous coding agents like Claude Code or Codex.
Premium Component Constraints: Guides the AI to use modern frontend techniques and minimalist aesthetics.
Framework Agnostic Concepts: Focuses on core design taste that can be applied across different web frameworks and libraries.
